To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the European responses to the Iraq intervention were shaped by different approaches to the international norms governing the use of force; (ii) the European responses can be classified into legal and moral positions; (iii) Germany’s and Poland’s positions are best characterized as legal; (iv) the UK’s position is best characterized as moral.

the diverging positions of the three European states on the Iraq intervention were based on distinct approaches to the use and interpretation of international norms and that these differences will make it difficult to develop a coherent European approach to the changing norms on the use of force.
The diverging European positions regarding the Iraq intervention reflected different approaches to the international norms regulating the use of military force.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the normative framework for military intervention.
the question of how the EU member states are responding to the changing norms regulating the use of military force.
how the changing norms of international intervention are affecting European states’ positions on the use of force.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single European foreign policy on the issue of military intervention.
the European Union has a moral obligation to intervene in cases of gross violations of human rights.
the European Union is a political entity, and not a military one, as the European Union has not been involved in military operations since 2003.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
European states are divided on the question of whether military intervention is legitimate if it is not authorized by the United Nations.
the European Union is not a unified actor when it comes to the use of military force.
the diverging views on the Iraq intervention are not only the result of different national interests, but reflect different understandings of what constitutes a legitimate use of force.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EU’s ability to act as a security provider in the future will depend on its capacity to develop a common approach to the use of armed force.
the European Union is unlikely to be able to develop a unified position in the future on issues of humanitarian intervention.
there are different approaches to the changing norms regulating military interventions.
